newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga begins restart of Vigdis oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Saga begins restart of Vigdis oilfield.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it had begun the process of restarting the North Sea Vigdis oilfield and hoped it would be up and running later today.
On Tuesday the company said it expected crude to flow from Vigdis on Wednesday. The restart, however, was taking longer than expected, Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said.
The development was closed down on May 23 after a gas leak was detected in the compressor train, which was traced to a design fault. It was originally expected to restart at the end of June.

"We are in the phase of putting it back in production but it is taking a little longer than expected because every signal has to be discussed with the manufacturer for verification," Schibevaag told Reuters.
"But hopefully we will have more news later today."
Vigdis, which came on stream in January, five months ahead of schedule, suffered an unscheduled shutdown on April 15 due to other problems with the gas compressor. The field was restarted on May 16.
Output was around 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) before the last incident, but peak production is planned to reach around 100,000 bpd.
Saga will close the field again for maintenance between August 25 and September 19 to coincide with a scheduled turnaround at the Gullfaks A platform. --Tanya Pang, Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
